test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 04 Sept, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the following sentence.

Shweta organises the sale of handmade pottery at a cheap rate.

options.text: Having one’s cake and eating it too
Making a fuss out of something

solution:
The correct answer is: **'****Go for a song****'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Go for a song"** means to be sold very cheaply. (बहुत सस्ते में बेचना)

 
 
• **Example:** The antique vase **went for a song** at the auction.
 
 
 
• **"Go for a song"** refers to selling something at a very low price, which aligns with the context of Shweta organizing the sale of handmade pottery at a cheap rate.

**​**Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Hush money** (चुप रहने के लिए दी गई रिश्वत): Money paid to someone to keep them silent about something.

 
 
• **Example:** The company paid **hush money** to the whistleblower to prevent the scandal from coming to light.
 
 
 
• **Having one’s cake and eating it too** (दोनों चीज़ें एक साथ चाहना): Trying to have two incompatible things at the same time.
 
 
• **Example:** You can't be in a relationship and flirt with others; that's **having one’s cake and eating it too**.
 
 
 
• **Making a fuss out of something** (किसी बात को लेकर हंगामा करना): Complaining or getting upset about something trivial.
 
 
• **Example:** She’s always **making a fuss out of nothing**; it's really annoying.
